fields.h1: Build a Geography Quiz That Shows Which Places People Miss
fields.hero_description: Build a geography quiz on any region, with right answers and score bands, and see which places each class or team missed.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Geography Quiz on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: A geography quiz checks what someone knows about places on a map. Emergent builds the questions and scoring, plus their table.
fields.feature_1:
Questions on the places you name

Name the region and the topic, such as the Great Lakes or European capitals, and Emergent writes each question with one right answer and three wrong ones from the same area.
fields.feature_2:
Score bands you set yourself

The quiz totals each player's right answers and shows the result for the band they land in, such as 7 or 8 of 8. Write each band's title and message, or ask Emergent to draft them.
fields.feature_3:
Answers tagged by region

Each answer is a row in a database you own, tagged with the player, the region, and the question. Group the rows by region to see which part of the map a class keeps missing.
fields.feature_4:
A phone screen for every question

Players answer one question per screen under a progress bar, so a team at a trivia table can play without zooming. Emergent puts no cap on how many people answer a quiz.
fields.feature_5:
Emails when a score falls short

Set a pass mark, and the app emails a teacher or trainer the names of anyone below it. Send a Slack alert to a channel instead when the whole staff needs to see the list.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your repository

Publish the quiz on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. Paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository, where a developer can extend it.

fields.tab_content_1:
Northeast questions trailed all 4 other regions

Vinton Middle School's 96 seventh graders, in 4 sections, take a 25-question US geography quiz, 5 questions per region. Each answer is saved with the student, the section, and the region. Only 259 of 480 Northeast answers were right, the lowest of the 5 regions. The team gave it 2 more days before the unit test.
fields.tab_content_2:
On trivia night, The Meridians scored 27 of 30

At Ostwick Public Library's world geography trivia night, 18 teams answered 30 questions on their phones, one per screen. Every answer was saved under the team's name. When the last round closed, The Meridians led with 27 of 30, 2 ahead of Due North, and the library read out the final standings before people left.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of 64 travelers, 39 missed the river through Budapest

Elsmere Rail Tours emails a 10-question Europe geography quiz to the 80 passengers on its 9-day Central Europe trip a week before departure. By day one, 64 of the 80 had taken it. The river through Budapest was missed by 39 of them, more than any other question, and the guide now opens the first talk with it.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any hire under 16 of 20 goes to Lupe Harlan

New dispatchers at Coldspring Freight take a 20-question geography quiz on states, interstates, and time zones in their first week. Anyone under 16 of 20 is named in an email to Lupe Harlan, the trainer. This month that was 3 of 11 new hires, and each one shadows a senior dispatcher for a shift.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Geography Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a geography quiz with fair questions and a results table that shows which places to review.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick one area and one audience
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add a reason under each answer
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the area the quiz covers, such as US state capitals or Europe's mountain ranges, and who takes it, such as a 7th-grade class or new staff. Put both in your prompt, and Emergent drafts questions pitched at that group.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Mix capitals, physical features like rivers and peaks, and borders on purpose. Tag each question with its region and its type as you write it. Those tags are what let the results table group answers by place once people start playing.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write the correct answer, then three wrong ones of the same kind from the same part of the map. A question about a European river should offer four European rivers. An option that is plainly off, like a city on another continent, gives the answer away.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Under each question, write one line that explains the answer and names where it comes from, such as a national park page or a government agency. Show those lines on the results screen. A teacher can then settle any answer a student disputes in seconds.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set the score bands before launch
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick 3 bands that suit the length, such as 0 to 3, 4 to 6, and 7 or 8 for an 8-question quiz, and write a short message for each. Check that every possible score lands in exactly one band before anyone plays.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Have 2 people from the real audience take the quiz on their phones before it goes out. Check that their answers land in the table with the right region tag, and rewrite any question that either of them read differently than you meant.
fields.howto_step_7_des: After the first round, sort the table by question and by region. Pick the 2 or 3 places missed most and open the next lesson, talk, or training shift with them. Then run the same questions again and compare the two rounds.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a geography quiz on US states and capitals for my 7th-grade social studies classes that scores every student.

faq_plan.a: A geography quiz is a set of questions that tests what someone knows about places: capitals and borders, along with the rivers and mountains between them. Each question has one right answer, and the score shows which parts of the map a player knows and which to study again.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a geography quiz?
faq_plan.a: Pick the region and the audience, then write each question with a correct option and three believable wrong ones, and set score bands. With Emergent's AI survey builder, you describe that quiz in a prompt and get a working app that scores every player and keeps each answer in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should a US geography quiz for middle school cover?
faq_plan.a: Cover states and capitals, the regions each state belongs to, major rivers and mountain ranges, and which states share a border. Write about 5 questions per region and tag each one with its region. The results then show which part of the country needs more class time, instead of one overall score.

faq_plan.q: What should a geography of America quiz cover?
faq_plan.a: It should cover the states, their capitals, and US landforms when America means the United States. When it means North America, add Canada, Mexico, and Central America. Say which one in the title, and pair the quiz with a vocabulary quiz on terms like delta, plateau, and isthmus.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep a world geography quiz from favoring one continent?
faq_plan.a: Set a count per continent before you write anything, such as 2 questions each for a 12-question world geography quiz, and tag every question with its continent. After the first round, compare results by continent. A continent far below the rest is the first place to look for a question that was too obscure.

faq_plan.q: Which countries should a Europe geography quiz include?
faq_plan.a: State the boundary in the intro first, such as every country from Iceland to the Ural Mountains. Then spread a geography quiz on Europe across every corner of the map, and include a few smaller countries like Slovenia or Moldova. That keeps the quiz from leaning only on the countries players already know.

faq_plan.q: What should I look for in a geography quiz maker?
faq_plan.a: Look for a score at the end, a results table you can sort by place, and questions that read well on a phone. A knowledge quiz scores right answers, while a personality-style quiz like a style quiz maps each answer to a result instead. Emergent sets no response cap, whether 10 players take the quiz or 10,000.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a geography quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Use 8 to 12 questions for a class warm-up or a quiz someone plays on a phone in one sitting, and 25 to 30 for a unit test or a full trivia night. Whatever the length, give each region the same number of questions, and the results will compare fairly across the map.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a world geography quiz harder for adults?
faq_plan.a: Move past capitals to physical features and less familiar places, such as mountain ranges and smaller countries. Ask which of two cities is farther north, or which country a river crosses first. Keep the wrong options close to the right one, because the difficulty should come from near misses, not trick wording.

faq_plan.q: How do I grade a geography quiz automatically?
faq_plan.a: Mark one option per question as correct and let the quiz count right answers when the player submits. On Emergent, the quiz is built from a prompt, and each graded answer is saved to a database you own. Every player's score and every miss is in one table, with no papers to mark.

quiz.title: Geography Quiz: 8 Questions on Oceans, Rivers, and Europe
quiz.intro: Eight questions on oceans, deserts, US rivers and lakes, and the mountains of Europe. Pick one answer for each; your score and a source for every answer show at the end.

questions.text: Which ocean basin is the largest on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific is both the largest and the deepest of the ocean basins.

source.quote: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of the world ocean basins

questions.text: What is the deepest known part of the ocean called?
questions.explanation: Challenger Deep lies beneath the western Pacific, at the southern end of the Mariana Trench.

source.quote: The deepest part of the ocean is called the Challenger Deep

questions.text: Which is the largest desert on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sahara is the largest hot desert, but Antarctica covers more ground and is the coldest desert on Earth.

source.quote: The largest desert on Earth is Antarctica, which covers 14.2 million square kilometers

questions.text: Which river is the longest in the United States?
questions.explanation: The Missouri runs more than 2,500 miles from near Three Forks, Montana, to the Mississippi at St. Louis.

source.quote: The Missouri is the longest river in the United States

questions.text: Which lake is the largest body of fresh water in the world by surface area?
questions.explanation: Lake Superior covers 31,700 square miles, about the size of Maine.

source.quote: Lake Superior is the largest body of fresh water in the world by surface area

questions.text: Which river runs through Grand Canyon National Park?
questions.explanation: The park takes in 278 miles of the Colorado River and the uplands beside it.

source.quote: the park encompasses 278 miles (447 km) of the Colorado River and adjacent uplands

questions.text: What is the highest peak in Europe?
questions.explanation: Mount Elbrus rises 5,642 meters (18,510 feet) in the Caucasus Mountains of Russia.

source.quote: Europe's highest peak, Mount Elbrus at 5,642 meters (18,510 feet), is in the Caucasus Mountains of Russia

questions.text: Which mountain range marks the eastern edge of Europe?
questions.explanation: Europe stretches from Iceland in the west to the Ural Mountains of Russia in the east.

source.quote: Europe extends from the island nation of Iceland in the west to the Ural Mountains of Russia in the east
